exposure: Pre-pregnancy BMI (underweight, normal weight, overweight, obese)
Small for gestational age (SGA) vs. non-small for gestational age (NSGA)
Birth weight (low birth weight, normal birth weight)
Gestational age at birth (extremely preterm, very preterm, moderate preterm, term)
cohort: 3,864 Southern Chinese women who gave first birth to a live singleton infant from January 2015 to December 2015
finding: Maternal overweight and obesity were associated with a significantly higher risk of gestational hypertension, cesarean delivery, and extremely preterm birth, while underweight was associated with an increased risk of low birth weight but a lower risk of gestational hypertension and cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Overweight and obese mothers had a higher risk of extremely preterm birth compared to normal-weight mothers, while underweight mothers had a lower risk of cesarean delivery.
